findings.checklist_item: Specify in AC5 that the new input_rejected signal must retain llm_unavailable's INDETERMINATE-and-never-sign semantics in all three readers (orchestrator.finalize_verdict, drift_floor recompute, review_bot coverage-gap), so an input-rejected degrade still fails-closed and is never signed as a PASS.
evidence: AC5: 'coverage.llm_unavailable boolean is True only for genuine LLMUnavailableError outages; LLMInputRejectedError instead sets a distinct input_rejected signal ... and the three readers ... are updated to read it'

orchestrator.py:468 `elif coverage.get("llm_unavailable"): verdict = "INDETERMINATE"` — the branch that both fails the review and prevents signing (fuel-posse-ball). drift_floor.py:212 and review_bot/adapter.py:114 similarly key off llm_unavailable.

gate_dispatch.py:203 and :560 catch (LLMUnavailableError, LLMInputRejectedError) in the SAME arm, both routed to _degraded_plan_review_verdict which currently sets llm_unavailable=True — so today an input-rejected degrade IS forced INDETERMINATE and unsigned.

ABSENCE: the plan states the readers 'read' input_rejected but never states input_rejected must retain the INDETERMINATE/no-sign semantics; an input-rejected review still did not complete, so a hollow PASS could be signed if the semantics are dropped.
findings.finding: AC5 splits coverage.llm_unavailable into a distinct input_rejected signal for LLMInputRejectedError but does not specify that input_rejected must still drive the INDETERMINATE verdict / no-sign / coverage-gap outcome that llm_unavailable currently produces, risking a hollow signed PASS.
scenarios: An LLMInputRejectedError degrade during review_plan/produce_code_review_verdict where, after the split, finalize_verdict no longer sees llm_unavailable and falls open to PASS, which review_plan then signs — a claim gate passes on a review that never ran.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend AC5 to require that finalize_verdict, drift_floor._recompute_verdict_after_drop, and review_bot/adapter._coverage_gap_reason treat input_rejected as an INDETERMINATE/coverage-gap cause equivalent to llm_unavailable (only the descriptive label and the code differ), so signing is still refused.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify, in AC5, the decision rule each of the three readers applies to `input_rejected`: the verdict finalize_verdict and _recompute_verdict_after_drop must emit (e.g. keep INDETERMINATE), and the review-bot's tag suffix (_TAG_SUFFIXES entry) plus whether the reason belongs in RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS (it should NOT, since input rejection is deterministic).
evidence: AC5 states LLMInputRejectedError 'instead sets a distinct `input_rejected` signal ... and the three readers (plan_review/drift_floor.py, plan_review/orchestrator.py, review_bot/adapter.py) are updated to read it' — but specifies no behavior per reader.

orchestrator.finalize_verdict (orchestrator.py:459-489) picks INDETERMINATE only via an explicit branch chain (prerequisite_indeterminate / config_fault / llm_unavailable / hierarchy_incomplete / verify_failed); a signal absent from that chain falls through to `verdict = 'PASS'` (line 489). Moving LLMInputRejectedError out of the llm_unavailable bucket without adding an input_rejected branch yields a hollow PASS — the very failure mode the epic's Problem section names.
drift_floor._recompute_verdict_after_drop (drift_floor.py:209-225) mirrors the same branch chain; it likewise defaults to PASS (line 225) when no known flag matches.

review_bot/adapter._coverage_gap_reason (adapter.py:107-119) returns a reason string that _message_tag looks up STRICTLY in _TAG_SUFFIXES (adapter.py:64-72, no `input_rejected` key → KeyError) and that is tested for retryability against RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS (adapter.py:82). LLMInputRejectedError's docstring (errors.py:51-67) states the input 'will be rejected identically every time, so waiting or retrying cannot help' — i.e. NON-retryable — so it must NOT inherit the retryable 'llm-unavailable' gap reason.

Confirmed LLMInputRejectedError actually reaches the degrade builders: `except (LLMUnavailableError, LLMInputRejectedError)` at gate_dispatch.py:203 and mid-run at 560, both calling _degraded_plan_review_verdict, which today hardcodes 'llm_unavailable': True (plan_review_recovery.py:462; gate_dispatch code-review builder at gate_dispatch.py:336).
findings.finding: AC5 introduces a new `input_rejected` coverage signal but does not define the verdict/vote decision rule the three named readers must apply to it, so an executor cannot know what each reader should DO with the new signal.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC5 (the gate-degrade coverage.llm_unavailable bullet); Scope: 'coverage.llm_unavailable boolean ... and its three readers'
scenarios: A plan-review degrade caused by a rejected/oversized prompt: with input_rejected replacing llm_unavailable and no new verdict branch, finalize_verdict returns PASS and review_plan would sign a hollow attestation.

The Gerrit review-bot processing a code-review verdict whose coverage carries input_rejected: _message_tag raises KeyError on the missing _TAG_SUFFIXES entry, or (if mapped to 'llm-unavailable') the bot treats a deterministic input rejection as a retryable defer and never fails-closed.
findings.suggested_fix: State that `input_rejected` retains INDETERMINATE in both verdict readers (add it to the branch chains alongside llm_unavailable), and in review_bot/adapter add a distinct non-retryable gap reason with its own _TAG_SUFFIXES entry (e.g. 'input-rejected' → 'BLOCK — coverage-gap (input-rejected)') deliberately excluded from RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS. Also define the exact key/value shape returned by the shared failure.degrade_cause_flags helper (which flag(s) it sets per exception type).
